h1: Fortune D Hotel Phitsanulok — Spacious, Good-Value Rooms in the City Centre, Steps from Wat Yai
intro: If you want a city-centre base in Phitsanulok with genuinely spacious, clean rooms that won't stretch the budget — Fortune D Hotel Phitsanulok is a name regulars keep coming back to · This 3-star, 78-room boutique sits on Saen Phon Phai Road in the Nai Mueang district, a short walk from Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) where you can pay respects to Phra Buddha Chinnarat, and not far from Central Plaza Phitsanulok · Guests consistently praise the 24-32 sqm rooms — larger than most hotels at this price — the friendly staff, and the free parking · Rooms start from approx. THB 900/night

body.html: Fortune D Hotel Phitsanulok opened in 2013 (formerly The Harmony Plus Apartment) on Saen Phon Phai Road, in a central spot that is walkable to Wat Yai and close to Central Plaza · It is a mid-size 78-room boutique under the Fortune Hotel Group, and its main draw is rooms that are larger than usual at an accessible price · Pilgrims visiting Phra Buddha Chinnarat, business travellers, and people passing through Phitsanulok on the way to Sukhothai often choose it for the value and the well-placed location.

Rooms of 24-32 sqm are genuinely spacious for this tier, decorated in warm tones with air conditioning, a fridge, flat-screen TV and a walk-in shower · The point guests echo most is that rooms are spacious, clean, the beds comfortable, and the value strong · That said, some reviews note that furnishings in certain rooms are starting to show their age with a little dust — it depends on the room you get, and a recently refreshed one feels noticeably better value.
"The room was much bigger than expected, clean, with a comfortable bed — hard to find this value in central Phitsanulok, and an easy morning walk to pay respects at Wat Yai."

Service is another strong point · Staff earn praise for being friendly and genuinely helpful, the front desk is open 24 hours, and there is a taxi-call service, luggage storage and laundry · The hotel has free private parking — a real convenience for self-drivers — plus an on-site restaurant and lobby bar · Breakfast is included in some packages and is fine to start the day, but several guests agree the selection is limited rather than a highlight of the stay.

The location is a real fit for exploring Phitsanulok · It is about a 6-minute walk to Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai), where you can pay respects to Phra Buddha Chinnarat and then stroll along the Nan River · Central Plaza Phitsanulok is under a 10-minute drive, and city markets and eateries are close by · The railway station is roughly a 20-minute walk (or a short drive) and the bus terminal about 10 minutes on foot · The hotel scores around 8.9 from 174 reviews on Trip.com and ranks near the top of the city's specialty lodging on TripAdvisor.

To be honest, Fortune D is not a luxury hotel and has no river view · The most common gripes are sound carrying between rooms (noise insulation), ageing furnishings in some rooms, and a few reviews mentioning pigeons on the balconies · If you want a Nan riverside room or a riverside-boutique mood, Dragon River Avenue or Grand Riverside may suit you better · But if you want a spacious, clean, central room within walking distance of the temple, close to Central Plaza, with free parking and a friendly budget — this delivers value that is hard to match in this part of town.

A tip from those who follow the reviews here: ask for a recently refreshed room on a higher floor away from the main corridor — it helps a lot with both noise and room condition · If you are driving, the free on-site parking is a genuine advantage in a city where spaces are scarce · And during festivals or long weekends when crowds come to honour Phra Buddha Chinnarat, book ahead because rooms fill quickly.

honestSummary: Fortune D is a strong pick in Phitsanulok for travellers who want a spacious, clean, central room within walking distance of Wat Yai, close to Central Plaza, at a friendly price · The roomy spaces and free parking are real strengths — but accept that sound still carries between rooms, some furnishings are ageing, and there is no river view.
honestChecks: If you want a Nan riverside room or a riverside-boutique mood — this is a city hotel with no water view → consider Dragon River Avenue or Grand Riverside in the same city instead.
If you are a light sleeper — reviews note some noise insulation issues between rooms → ask for a higher-floor room away from the main corridor and pack ear plugs just in case.
If you expect a varied breakfast — the spread here is fairly limited, filling but not a highlight → keep expectations modest, or head out for noodles and local eats nearby.

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Fortune D Hotel Phitsanulok

faq.q: Where is Fortune D Hotel Phitsanulok, and can you walk to Wat Yai?
faq.a: It is at 40 Saen Phon Phai Road, Nai Mueang, in central Phitsanulok · It's about a 6-minute walk to Wat Phra Si Rattana Mahathat (Wat Yai) to honour Phra Buddha Chinnarat · Central Plaza Phitsanulok is under a 10-minute drive · The bus terminal is roughly a 10-minute walk and the railway station is close by · Phitsanulok Airport is about a 15-minute drive.

faq.q: How much does Fortune D Hotel Phitsanulok cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Rooms start from approx. THB 900/night for a Superior room of 24-32 sqm · A more recently refreshed Deluxe runs around THB 1,200 · A Family Suite suited to families is around THB 1,600 · Prices vary by season and platform, so always compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Who is Fortune D Hotel Phitsanulok best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for travellers who want a spacious, clean, central room within walking distance of Wat Yai, close to Central Plaza, at a friendly price · The roomy spaces and free parking are the standout features · Ideal for self-drivers, business travellers, or people passing through Phitsanulok on the way to Sukhothai who prioritise value over a river view.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Fortune D really spacious and clean?
faq.a: Rooms of 24-32 sqm are genuinely spacious for this tier, and cleanliness is the point guests consistently praise · However, condition varies by renovation cycle — some rooms have ageing furnishings and a little dust · It's worth asking for a recently refreshed room when booking or at check-in for noticeably better value.

faq.q: Does it have parking and breakfast?
faq.a: Yes — there is free private parking, a real convenience in a city where spaces are scarce · Breakfast is included in some packages and is fine to start the day, though many guests find the selection limited · There is also an on-site restaurant and lobby bar, a 24-hour front desk, and a taxi-call service.

faq.q: Is there noise between rooms, and how should I book?
faq.a: There are reviews mentioning sound carrying between rooms (noise insulation) and pigeons on some balconies — ask for a higher-floor room away from the main corridor and pack ear plugs just in case · During festivals or long weekends when crowds come to honour Phra Buddha Chinnarat, rooms fill quickly, so book ahead and choose a free-cancellation rate.
